subject: Next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing, latency window & token mix
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchidretail.com>, Procurement <procurement@orchidretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing, latency window & token mix

Hi Sanjay / procurement team —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a compact list of inputs we need to produce a firm Dedicated capacity recommendation (GPU mix, reserved pool size, and latency SLOs). I copied Rachel and Ben so we can coordinate pricing and the canary/rollout plan.

What we discussed / what we need from you:
- Peak TPS target (requests/sec) and expected 95th pctl latency SLO (ms) for inference.
- Typical concurrency per user session and peak concurrent sessions.
- Token mix: average prompt tokens, average response tokens, and % of short classification calls (<=64 tokens).
- Which deployment modes are must-haves: Hosted API / Dedicated reserved capacity / Private VPC / On-prem. If Private VPC is required, any constraints on IP ranges or cloud provider?
- Any regulatory/security must-haves (SOC2, PCI, data residency).
- Timeline for go-live and whether you'd consider a canary (2–4 week) on Hosted first.

Attached: Orchid_capacity_workbook.xlsx and a sample_token_profile.json — please populate the workbook with the TPS/concurrency rows and token mix so we can run sizing scenarios.

Initial notes from our side (high-level):
- For a workload with medium tokens (prompt ~100, response ~400) and 100–150 peak TPS, we typically recommend a reserved pool using H100s for best latency headroom; A100s can be more cost-efficient for steady lower-latency-acceptable workloads.
- Prefix/KV caching will heavily change unit economics if >30% of calls share prefixes; we can size a smaller pool if caching reduces per-request work.
- We have batching knobs that trade throughput for latency; please include target P95 latency so we can select an SLO-aware configuration.

Next steps: once you return the workbook, we'll run three scenarios (cost-optimized A100 pool, latency-optimized H100 pool, and a hybrid mix) and share a provisional SKU estimate.

If Private VPC is a hard requirement, call that out in the workbook so we route to our Private onboarding team early.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if helpful.

—
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments (2): Orchid_capacity_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample_token_profile.json (json)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchidretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orchidretail.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing, latency window & token mix

Markus —

Thanks for the recap and the workbook. I filled the high-level numbers below and uploaded a signed security questionnaire (attached). A few clarifications:

- Traffic profile: peak TPS we expect ~120 requests/sec (spiky marketing windows), steady-state ~25–35 TPS.
- Concurrency: we expect ~4 concurrent requests per user session on average; peak concurrent sessions ~900.
- Token mix: avg prompt = 80 tokens, avg response = 450 tokens (some long-form regeneration); ~60% of calls are long generation, ~30% are short classification (<64 tokens), ~10% are embeddings.
- Latency SLO: target P95 tail < 250 ms for the classification/short calls; for long generations we're OK with P95 < 1.2s but would like median under 400ms if possible.
- Deployment mode: we need Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private VPC (VPC peering to our AWS account) — Private is a hard requirement because of PII in prompts. Hosted API is acceptable only for canary/test.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II is required; procurement will push additional clauses on data retention.
- Timeline: hoping for pilot in Q4; procurement needs a preliminary cost worksheet for internal sign-off.

Question for you: given this mix (high % long generations + a large slug of short classification calls with strict P95), do you have a recommended GPU baseline (A100 vs H100) and a sense for whether a hybrid pool makes sense? Also, do you recommend adding a hot KV cache layer for prompt prefixes?

Attached: security_questionnaire.pdf. I also updated the capacity workbook with the numbers (Orchid_capacity_workbook.xlsx).

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of AI Product | Orchid Retail
sanjay@orchidretail.com | +1 212-555-0147

Attachments (1): security_questionnaire.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchidretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing, latency window & token mix

Sanjay —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the filled workbook. Based on what you sent, here are our provisional recommendations and the immediate asks so we can finalize SKU/math: 

1) GPU recommendation (baseline):
- Hybrid approach looks best for your mixed workload. Reserve a small H100 pool (e.g., 2x H100 nodes) dedicated to low-latency short classification requests — this keeps P95 < 250ms for those calls.
- Add an A100 pool (3–4x A100) sized for sustained throughput to handle the long generation workload more cost-effectively. The A100s will be paired with longer batching windows for throughput.

2) Concurrency / TPS sizing:
- With avg prompt 80 / avg response 450: peak 120 TPS with caching disabled requires the hybrid above to avoid P95 degradation. If you can enable prefix/KV caching for the 30% repeated prompts, you get ~30–40% fewer GPU ops and can reduce the A100 count by ~1 node.
- Recommend keeping target concurrency headroom at 1.5–2× expected concurrent sessions for autoscaling buffer.

3) Latency & batching tradeoffs:
- We'll tune batching knobs per pool: H100 pool configured for tight latency windows (batch window <= 6ms, small batch sizes), A100 pool with slightly larger batch windows to maximize token throughput.

4) Private VPC & security:
- Private VPC is feasible — we will need your AWS account ID and preferred region, and our Private onboarding team will initiate the peering/KMS paperwork. SOC2 Type II is in place at Redwood; I'll have our security lead send the attestation and common redlines.

5) Next deliverables from us by end of week once you confirm the workbook:
- Provisional SKU estimate (I attached provisional_sku_estimate.pdf).
- Canary plan: 2-week Hosted pilot followed by a 30-day reserved pool ramp plan.
- Ops runbook for autoscaling thresholds and rollback.

Ben and Rachel — can you confirm discount thresholds for a 12-month reserved commitment and whether we can offer an accelerated onboarding credit for Private deployments?

Sanjay — quick Q: can procurement also share the retention window you need for prompt/response artifacts? That will affect cost and compliance gating.

Happy to jump on a brief call to walk through the SKU math.

—
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com

Attachments (1): provisional_sku_estimate.pdf
